steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: In a place far, far away, there once was a village where the people led happy lives.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Some built homes to shelter the others from the elements, some reclaimed farmland.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Others set out to hunt, search for ores, and at the same time, fought back scoundrels who would take the village for themselves.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: No concept of ego existed among those villagers, no difference between self and other. No one could survive without the rest. They lived together in that small village, and called it home.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: But, nothing good lasts forever. The soil yielded less and less, hunting become more and more difficult, and as food dwindled, stomachs grumbled in hunger.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: The cold months crept closer and closer, but there was not enough fuel for heat...

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Something had to be done about this! And so everyone said, 'this must be a trial given to us by the Lord, and we must pray for forgiveness!'

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Just at that time, a group of well-meaning people came by, and upon seeing the plight of the village, spoke to the head of the villagers:

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: 'Come live with us in our city.'

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: 'But we can only bring those who are most like us.'

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: 'Come, and enjoy a better life. All you need to do is leave a few of you behind.'

steps.name: Lively Child
steps.text: I don't like this story, Seniora Arturia!

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Hmm? Why not?

steps.name: Lively Child
steps.text: Starving is really bad, it hurts!

steps.name: Shy Child
steps.text: Yeah, it's bad, and so is leaving your friends behind...

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Yes, that is a very 'correct' idea of collectivism, with a little bit of heroism mixed in... or even romanticism.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Romantic stories do have ways of stirring the heart, but it is exactly that romanticism and high-mindedness that has a way of confounding others. Naturally, neither you nor I are immune.

steps.name: Shy Child
steps.text: Ugh, big words... I don't get it at all...

steps.name: Lively Child
steps.text: You're talking like a weirdo again, Seniora Arturia!

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Oh no, I'm sorry. That's my mistake.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Let's go with a different story then. What would you like to hear?

steps.name: Lively Child
steps.text: I wanna hear... a hero story!

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: You all want to become heroes?

steps.name: Shy Child & Lively Child
steps.text: I wanna be a great hero! Just like Mamma!

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Wow, your mamma sounds amazing!

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Be good now, and give me just a moment.

steps.name: Gentle Priest
steps.text: I seem to have caught you at a bad time. Am I interrupting you, Arturia?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: You ask despite already knowing, Most Reverend Bishop Aulus.

steps.name: Aulus
steps.text: Apologies. It was not my intent to displease you. I merely came to bid you farewell.

steps.name: Aulus
steps.text: Owing to the addition of an unexpected traveling companion, I plan to leave as soon as possible and escort my companion back home.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Allow me to offer a prayer for this pitiful soul.

steps.name: Aulus
steps.text: I'm not trying to fight with you here...

steps.name: Aulus
steps.text: ...especially not in front of the children.

steps.name: Aulus
steps.text: However, 'pitiful' should never be used to describe one's resolve to live.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Resolve, hm... resolve.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: The amount of control we have over our own lives is often not as perfect as we believe it to be, and no one is ever the wiser until proven otherwise.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Think of things that one must never do. They are often already done by the time their senses return to them.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Does the act of blame contradict the heart's inner desires? Who is to say that our so-called resolve is not just a coping mechanism used to deceive ourselves?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: At times like these, where are our truest emotions and intentions hidden?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: When will the day come that one's thoughts, emotions, and actions can truly be unified?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Is this not the point of your inquiry, sir?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: It seems that today is a in which a great many things will unfold. I hear a commotion outside, as if some acquaintances have come knocking.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: If I were you, Bishop Aulus, I would not be in such a hurry to leave just yet.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Sorry to keep you waiting.

steps.name: Lively Child
steps.text: You took forever, Seniora Arturia!

steps.name: Shy Child
steps.text: So slow...

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Please forgive me. Why don't I tell an extra spectacular story to make up for it?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Do you want to hear a story of a grand battle between heroes and villains?

steps.name: Shy Child & Lively Child
steps.text: I do, I do!

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Alright. Then, you must listen carefully.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: A long, long time ago in a faraway castle, there lived a young boy. The boy didn't express much emotion and rarely spoke, but he was incredibly fierce in a fight...

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: I told you I'm just a hunter. If that's not enough to satisfy you, then I don't mind trying something else.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: I'm just an ordinary, roughly middle-aged Sarkaz.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I do not believe that is the entire truth.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: That weapon behind you, you carry it always. You actively conceal your movements, which is a mercenary's habit.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: That's for self-defense.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: You saw it yourself. Those bandits are always raiding us. Things aren't so peaceful here.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: That does not explain why you have a mercenary's habit.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: I've got farm equipment in my hands more often than weapons these days.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: I hunt for a living here. Sometimes, I work in the fields, or in the mines when I have to.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: No need to get all excited about these old hands of mine. I'm just an ordinary guy, bound up by life.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Federico, stay mindful of our mission here.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: I don't think now's the time to be chasing hypotheticals.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: A reasonable determination.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Would Your Excellency mind explaining the situation?

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Sorry to bring you trouble, Stefano.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: No, you have nothing to apologize for, Gerald.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: As the two of you might surmise...

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Over a decade ago, Gerald brought a small group of Sarkaz to the monastery. At the time, they were stranded in the barrens, without food or ammunition.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: When they found our monastery, they had no choice but to try to make contact.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You didn't expel them, so they chose to settle here.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Is there a difference between driving out those who've been cornered, and driving them into a corner yourself?

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Er, I guess that makes sense...

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: At first, not everyone was accepting of our new neighbors.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: But rootless hatred and prejudice have no purchase when survival is at stake.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: We provided a place for these people to stay, and in turn, they helped us deal with our own problems.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Our food shortage, the bandit threat, and our gradually depleting energy supply...

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: They relied on us, so we also relied on them.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: But you still chose to send Messengers to contact Laterano.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: A choice made in the absence of choice...

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Laterano is willing to provide us with assistance, and is also willing to welcome us back in.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: However, even Lemuen, the nuncio willing to grant us the most concessions, still held one non-negotiable condition–

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: 'Sarkaz have no place in Paradise.'

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: No place? Why?!

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: On the basis of race alone? Just because they are Sarkaz?!

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: How are they any different from us? Without these stalwart brothers and sisters, we would've lost our fight for survival long ago!

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Where was Laterano during all that time we were supporting each other?!

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: So, let me beg the two of you, to once again–

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Plead to the wisdom of His Holiness the Pope, and to your faith...
The haggard old man raises both his hands.
He both appears to be holding up his faith, as well as crumbling beneath its overwhelming weight.
The Sankta's faith is formless, intangible, nowhere to be found.
His fingers grasp for the halo above his head in vain, the old man's hands gradually slipping until they cover his face.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: What Lemuen said is correct. There will not be Sarkaz in Laterano.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Nor will Laterano allow any Sarkaz through her gates.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Hey, Federico, you don't have to be so blunt.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: This is a fact.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Enough, Stefano.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: I already told you. We can accept it.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: You go to Laterano, and we'll find a place to start over. That nuncio, Lemuen, promised us some support. But in name... we have to go our separate ways.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: It's always been a fact. The fact that they even offered us that much is already more than I expected. It's more than enough.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: No, it shouldn't be a fact! It's certainly not enough!

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Don't get it? That we even nominally have to go our separate ways only makes this all the more ridiculous!

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Sorry, Stefano.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: We've given up.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: What do you mean?

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: What I mean is, you don't have to subject yourself to all this, just for our sake.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: You don't need to be so hard on yourself.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: I've talked to the others. We've decided... we're leaving.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: What are you saying...?

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: I assume that settles things, Reverend Executors?

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: We'll leave. It just means letting go of a group of destitute refugees. You can do that, right?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The Notarial Hall does not harm innocent civilians.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: I'm glad.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Really, Federico?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I do not lie.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Umm... How should I put this... Well, whatever. You're leading this operation, so if that's what you've decided, I don't object.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: I swear to you, a Sarkaz has never been in a Lateran sacrarium.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: That in itself does not constitute a crime.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Really now?

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: How should I say this... There's actually no explicit prohibition on it.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Bishop Stefano Torregrossa, I will continue to pursue the whereabouts of Oren Argiolas, based on your testimony.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: May I take it that you've accepted the conditions put forth by the Lateran, that all monastery residents, with the exception of the Sarkaz, will be resettled in Laterano at a later date?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: If you remain silent, I will interpret that as your tacit consent.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Stefano.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Time...

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: I need a bit more time...

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: I would finish my final sermon, and spend one last night here.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Please... give me just a bit more time at the very end.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: I will give you an answer after Matins tomorrow.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: What do you think, Federico?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Fine.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Now, I wish to meet with Cardinal Aide Lemuen.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Seniora Lemuen is our guest. Of course you may visit her, if you wish.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Understood.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: In that case, we will take our leave... Hey, wait a second! At least say something first, Federico!

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Am I still holding onto some of my old merc habits?

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Looks like even after all these years, some habits die hard.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Gerald, are you absolutely certain of this?

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Sure, Stefano. You know I wouldn't joke around with this stuff.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: We're all bound by the need to survive.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: What you said was no lie.

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: Anyone home? I brought your winter clothes!

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: Huh, that's weird... Where is everybody today?

steps.name: Sarkaz Resident
steps.text: Fina? What are you doing standing around here?

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: Oh, Caroline! Perfect timing!

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: I came by to drop off everyone's winter clothes, but is something going on? I've been walking around all day and haven't seen a soul... What are you all busy with?

steps.name: Caroline
steps.text: We... have some stuff to take care of.

steps.name: Caroline
steps.text: Thanks for coming all the way out here, but we're fine with what we have. Err, we already have enough winter clothes, so you can take these back. Also, tell the others not to worry about us.

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: What are you talking about? When in the last few years have any of us had enough to get through the winter?

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: Aren't you still wearing that light coat, Caroline? The temperature's going to drop pretty soon, so we need to get you into something a bit thicker...

steps.name: Caroline
steps.text: Fina, is something wrong?

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: What's that in your hand?

steps.name: Caroline
steps.text: Oh... It's nothing. Just some hardtack.

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: No, let me see it!

steps.name: Caroline
steps.text: Hey, wait!
The Sankta girl reaches out to snatch the supposed hardtack from behind the other girl's back. Almost instinctively, she splits the dry, hard thing down the middle before she is pushed away.
Stuffed inside the hardtack are truths hidden away all this time, finally exposed to her eyes.

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: What... is this?

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: Bran... and sawdust?!

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: Caroline?!

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: Didn't you say you had more than enough food? Then... why are you eating this?

steps.name: Caroline
steps.text: No, Fina, listen to me. We, we're just...

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: Just what?

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: Talk to me, Caroline.

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: Tell me... What depths have we stooped to these days?
Knock.
Knock. Knock, knock. Knock, knock, knock.
The sound of knuckles rapping at the door.
The door isn't actually locked, but the guests outside still continue to knock and wait for a response.
This used to be a secret code agreed upon by several friends from school. So much time has passed that Lemuen thought she forgot, but the facts prove that she has not forgotten.
The meaning of the code words tapped by the guests is:
'Rescue successful.'
And: 'First arrival.'

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Come in.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Salve, room service.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Gratias, please put the food over there on the table. Do you need a tip?

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: You can't just ask if you need to tip. It's gotta come from the heart, right?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Hmm, I guess you have a point.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: You don't seem surprised at all, Lemuen.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Are you disappointed that it's me?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Of course not.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: The fact that you're here means news of this place has already reached Laterano, right?

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Hmm? Well, more or less. That Oren guy actually left you behind and ran off by himself. When I get back, I'm going to tell Mostima and Fiammetta.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Ahaha. Cut him some slack, won't you?

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Booooo...

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Alright then, back to business. I know His Holiness wouldn't send you here alone, which means...

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: I need you to report your mission, as well as who's with you.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Switched to your business voice, huh? Alright then, Cardinal Aide Lemuen.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: This mission was commissioned directly by His Holiness and is led by Federico, executor of the Notarial Hall. The other functionary is Richele Colombo, another executor who volunteered to come.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Our first objective is to locate you and Oren, and the second is to investigate this monastery.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Oh right, Federico also has another mission to maintain order. Unfortunately, I think His Holiness picked the wrong guy for the job this time.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: And that concludes my report.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Mmhmm... I see. So, His Holiness actually sent that Federico, huh...

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Okay. I get the gist of things. Gratias, Ria.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Again with the nicknames... C'mon, you should know better.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: So, what are you going to do next? On the surface, it looks like your movements are being restricted, but in fact, it's you who doesn't want to leave, right?

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: If you wanted to leave, nobody here could stop you.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: My legs aren't fully healed yet.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Like that makes a difference.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: You trust me too much, Ria, though I suppose that's fine... Alright. It's true that I decided to stay behind.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: If Federico is trying to arrest the bishop here on charges of false imprisonment, I'd appreciate it if you could clear up the situation for me.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Also, sorry... But I don't plan on leaving just yet.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Mind if I ask why?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: The reason... Hmm. Let's just say that diplomacy isn't something that can be settled with guns and bullets alone.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: When it comes to a shootout, the odds are always in my favor. But if I have to sit down for a negotiation, I need to tread carefully or I might end up persuaded by the other party.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: It just so happens that I get along quite well with the residents here, so I want to see who ends up changing their mind first.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Oh? When you put it that way, it sounds like you plan on compromising.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Back in school, you watched me for an entire year just to make sure I showed up to class!

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Heehee. I thought it'd be a shame if you couldn't get your diploma for attendance reasons.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: As for the problem we have here... I still have a friendly attitude at least, right?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: I knew Oren would report the situation here, which is why I chose to stay behind. I've had a bad feeling about it, and I don't want to provoke the bishop any further...

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: With all the information I have on the monastery now, if there ever arises another opportunity to sit down at the negotiation table, I may be able to get him to relax a little and accept my proposal.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: *sigh*. I thought you'd say as much.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: I'm glad you understand.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: That's not what I said.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: But that's what you're thinking.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: I kinda hate empathy sometimes.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Now now, don't talk like that. How much do you know about the situation here?

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Enough.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Nothing special about it other than the group of Sarkaz.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Did you know they sent a total of three Messengers?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: ...Lia.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: I had the impression that you've never liked field missions. What made you sign up for this one?

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Maybe that I wanted to see you?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Liar, liar~

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Anyway, I'll find the others and explain your situation first.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: But to be entirely honest, I don't think what you're doing here is going to accomplish anything.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: ...It's worth a shot.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: *sigh*, you're getting scarier and scarier, Lemuen.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Not like it matters, though...

steps.name: Familiar Male Voice
steps.text: Finally mustered the means to reach out to me?

steps.name: Familiar Male Voice
steps.text: Here I thought you'd abandon the mission after seeing Lemuen.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Who knows, might not work out.

steps.name: Familiar Male Voice
steps.text: No joke, please. Spare me.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: You brought it up.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Alright, I don't have time to chat either. Let's talk business.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Phew... Dealing with guys like him really wears you down...

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: What a pain in the ass, this mission. Never would've taken it, if I knew.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Huh? Who's there?!

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Woah, didn't think you'd actually follow me, girly.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: I, I can't have you running around the monastery by yourself! I need to keep an eye on you to make sure you don't do anything bad!

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: And, uh...

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: There's also a favor I'd like to ask of you... and of course I'll pay you back for it!

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Um, let's see...

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Flour, eggs...

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: And, uh... Where's the leftover sugar from last time...?

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Ugh, I've been trying so hard to scrounge up leftover ingredients from dinner ever day, so why is there still so little?

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: I need enough for Serpilia, Avus Stefano, Fina, and Raimund... And also, Patruus Gerald, Patruus Clément, Seniora Caroline, and...

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: There's not going to be enough though.

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: Tuna?

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: I'm coming in, okay? There's something I have to tell you... What are you doing in here?

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Oh, Fina! I was just about to go look for you!

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Do you still remember when I helped Amita Nina with farm work for a month? Where did I put that bit of white sugar I got in return?

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: How long ago was that? Where are you going now?

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: What do you need sugar for? And, where'd you get all those cooking ingredients?

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: Wait, Tuna... Don't tell me you're still trying to bake sweets, at a time like this...?

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Um, Fina, what's wrong? Are you... mad at me?

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: I wasn't trying to hide food from you! I just wanted to prepare a surprise for everyone. Fina, don't be mad at me, okay? I promise you'll be the first to have some after I'm done!

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: Tuna, you... Forget it, just put those things down. Now's not the time to be doing stuff like this!

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Huh? But...

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: But what?

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: But, I promised someone I'd make a herb pizzella as a gift...

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: ...A gift?

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Yeah! She helped fix up my patron firearm, so I have to thank her!

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: It's like a miracle, Fina! Once this gun got fixed, I felt something different about it just holding it in my hands! It's like... like I knew how to use it from birth!

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Look! It's even prettier now, and the two of us will be able to use it together from now on!

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: You know what, Tuna...?

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: I actually never cared that much about my own firearm. Or for Avus Stefano's sermons.

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: I don't even care that I've never seen Laterano.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Fina, what are you talking about?

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: Can I even really be called a Sankta?

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: Maybe I can.

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: But, I care about you, and Raimund, and Avus Stefano and Patruus Gerald. And Patruus Clément, Amita Nina, Caroline...

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: I care about everyone here. This is my only home, and they are my only family.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: What are you talking about, Fina? Of course I care about everyone else, just like you–

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: No, it's not the same!

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: If you were just like me...

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: If you knew how hard Raimund and the others have it, then you wouldn't be in the mood to make your joke of a pizzella at a time like this! You wouldn't be so naïve!

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: I kinda feel like you changed after those people from Laterano showed up.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Huh? Of course I haven't...

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: Tuna, that gun of yours... Was Lemuen the Lateran who fixed it up for you?

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Your Excellency, I've allowed the two visitors freedom of movement around the monastery, as you ordered.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: But, are you sure it's alright? You... You don't look too good. Do you want to get some rest first?

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Oh, Clément, it's nothing you need to worry about.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Go ring the bell. This week's sermon is being moved to today, so go tell the others...

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Gerald, are you and your people coming?

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Sorry, Stefano. We still have a lot to prepare. I can't say how many of us will show.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: I understand.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Are we seriously going to accept their terms? Do we absolutely have to leave behind our own?

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Enough.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Go, Clément. Hurry.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Alright...

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: If faith has betrayed itself, then I, too, must make my decision...

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: I must repent.
